title: Path Aggregation Network for Instance Segmentation
venue: IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings - IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings

problem.summary: In Mask R-CNN/FPN pipelines information propagation is suboptimal: low-level localization signals must travel a very long path to reach the topmost features, each proposal is heuristically locked to a single feature level, and mask prediction is made from a single view.
statements: There is a long path from low-level structure to topmost features, making accurate localization hard to access.
Each proposal is pooled from one feature level assigned heuristically, discarding information in other levels.
Mask prediction is made on a single view, losing the chance to gather more diverse information.
Target datasets contain blur, heavy occlusion and extremely small instances.

evidence.quote: But there is a long path from low-level structure to topmost features, increasing difficulty to access accurate localization information.
Further, each proposal is predicted based on feature grids pooled from one feature level, which is assigned heuristically.
Finally, mask prediction is made on a single view, losing the chance to gather more diverse information.
For example, two proposals with 10-pixel difference can be assigned to different levels.

background.summary: PANet is built on Mask R-CNN with an FPN feature pyramid, drawing on network-design principles of short information paths (residual/dense connections) and parallel paths, and it notes that prior multi-level fusion methods (ION, Hypernet, Hypercolumn) require complicated normalization-concatenation-reduction sequences.

evidence.quote: The way that information propagates in neural networks is of great importance.
There have been several principles proposed for designing networks in image classification that are also effective for object recognition.
We take FPN as a baseline and much enhance it.

solution.summary: PANet boosts information flow in proposal-based instance segmentation with three components: bottom-up path augmentation that carries low-level localization signals up the pyramid, adaptive feature pooling where every proposal pools from all feature levels and fuses them, and a fully-connected branch fused with the FCN mask prediction.
solution.approach: Augment FPN with a bottom-up path of lateral connections from P2 to P5, let each proposal pool and max-fuse features from every level, and combine FCN mask predictions with a complementary fc-branch prediction.
components: bottom-up path augmentation producing feature maps N2-N5
adaptive feature pooling with ROIAlign and element-wise max/sum fusion
fully-connected fusion branch added to the mask prediction path
heavier head with 4 shared 3x3 convolutions for box prediction

evidence.quote: we propose Path Aggregation Network (PANet) aiming at boosting information flow in proposal-based instance segmentation framework.

we enhance the entire feature hierarchy with accurate localization signals in lower layers by bottom-up path augmentation, which shortens the information path between lower layers and topmost feature.
We present adaptive feature pooling, which links feature grid and all feature levels to make useful information in each feature level propagate directly to following proposal subnetworks.
A complementary branch capturing different views for each proposal is created to further improve mask prediction.
we build a path with clean lateral connections from the low level to top ones.

experiments.summary: PANet is evaluated on COCO (mask and box AP), Cityscapes and MVD against Mask R-CNN+FPN, the COCO 2016 champions, RetinaNet and others, with a component-by-component ablation on val-2017; it entered and won the COCO 2017 instance segmentation challenge.

evidence.quote: Our PANet reaches the 1st place in the COCO 2017 Challenge Instance Segmentation task and the 2nd place in Object Detection task without large-batch training.
With all these components in PANet, improvement on mask AP is 4.4 over baselines.
we achieve 9.1% absolute and 24% relative improvement on instance segmentation

limitations.summary: The paper states no limitations section; however roughly half of its COCO gain comes from multi-scale training and synchronized batch normalization rather than the proposed architecture, the top challenge numbers rely on ensembles, DCN and testing tricks, and proposals come from a separately trained RPN.
items: About half of the total improvement comes from multi-scale training and multi-GPU synchronized batch normalization, not from the PANet components.
The 46.7 AP challenge result requires deformable convolutions, testing tricks, larger models and an ensemble.
Proposals are produced by an independently trained RPN, so the backbone is not shared with the detection/segmentation network.
Fully-connected fusion adds only 0.7 mask AP, and the heavier head helps mainly the multi-task box branch.

evidence.quote: Half improvement is from multi-scale training and multiGPU sync. BN, which are effective strategies to help train better models.
such as multi-scale testing, horizontal flip testing, mask voting and box voting, are adopted.
proposals are from an independently trained RPN [35, 51] for convenient ablation and fair comparison, i.e., the backbone is not shared with object detection/instance segmentation.

futureDirections.direction: Extend PANet from images to video and RGBD data.
futureDirections.quote: Our future work will be to extend our method to video and RGBD data.

applications.domain: autonomous vehicles, robotics and video surveillance
applications.detail: The authors motivate instance segmentation as a task that widely benefits autonomous vehicles, robotics and video surveillance, and evaluate on street-scene datasets (Cityscapes, MVD) captured by car-mounted cameras.
applications.quote: This task widely benefits autonomous vehicles, robotics, video surveillance, to name a few.

deploymentClaims: The proposed components are simple to implement and add only subtle extra computational overhead.
The framework reached 1st place in COCO 2017 instance segmentation and 2nd place in object detection without large-batch training.

evidence.quote: These improvements are simple to implement, with subtle extra computational overhead.
Our framework reaches the 1st place in Instance Segmentation task and the 2nd place in Object Detection task without large-batch training.
